narrative: Global markets are experiencing a pronounced tech-led selloff driven by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's sudden resignation and tightened US export curbs on remote AI chip access to China. Monetary policy headwinds are compounding equity pressure as Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack advocated for continuing restrictive policy to tame sticky inflation, pushing 2-year Treasury yields up 30 basis points. Concurrently, investor focus is centered on immediate AI capital expenditure viability ahead of Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's multi-billion-dollar Nasdaq IPO. Commodities are facing broad pressure, with crude oil sliding over 3% amid expectations of future supply imbalances and gold softening against higher bond yields.

Nasdaq.why: Heavy selling pressure led by semiconductors following widened US export curbs, Nvidia's leadership crisis, and valuation multiple compression cited by Charlie Pellett and J.P. Coviello.

S&P 500.why: Charlie Pellett notes the index dropped over 1.7% as tech weakness, rising yields, and restrictive Fed expectations offset broader consumer strength cited by PIMCO's Tony Crescenzi.

Gold.why: Charlie Pellett reports gold fell 0.79% to $3,853.93 per ounce under pressure from elevated 10-year Treasury yields holding at 5.11%.

Oil.why: WTI and Brent dropped over 3% to $85.57 and $92.58 respectively (Charlie Pellett), dragged down by potential 2027 supply glut forecasts and Chevron expanding Venezuelan output to nearly 300,000 bpd.

priced_in: Prolonged restrictive Federal Reserve policy with roughly three 25 bps rate hikes over the next six months
Consensus next-12-month equity earnings growth of approximately 18%
Tech multiple de-rating driven by AI export restrictions and proposed PERM foreign labor sponsorship rules
Nvidia exceeding third-quarter consensus earnings estimates despite near-term leadership uncertainty
Long lead times for frontier AI labs to achieve free cash flow positivity, with estimates stretching to 2030
debates: Broader equity resilience vs tech fragility: Tony Crescenzi (PIMCO) and Barry Ritholtz argue US consumer strength and non-tech sectors remain resilient, whereas J.P. Coviello highlights multiple compression from persistent 5.5% super-core services inflation
AI debt and capex sustainability: William Dudley warns of systemic leverage risks tied to AI financing, contrasting with strong market demand for Anthropic's IPO
Oil market balance: Washington Post's Tara Copp points to elevated Middle East geopolitical risk premiums, while anchors highlight potential upcoming supply gluts and Chevron's Venezuelan ramp
